answer.text: Today’s rules leave $3,018,933 of $3,354,370 in free cash to Town Meeting; the draft leaves $924,030. The calculator applies either rule set, or any other.

blocks.alt: Conclusions from the financial policy pages, each linked to its page

points.text: The draft’s minimums claim $2,430,340 of $3,354,370 in free cash, 72% of it.
The draft sets 9 of 16 dials by rule that today’s policies leave open or set lower.
General stabilization rose from 4.44% of the budget in FY2017 to 6.24% in FY2025.
Free cash landed inside the draft’s five to seven percent in 3 of 11 certifications.
The trust has grown every year since FY2017, to $1,736,976 against a liability of $57,398,019.
Paying the full actuarially determined contribution would have taken $1,943,838 more in FY2025.
The 22 titles on the 3 December 2026 agenda match the April 2024 draft’s, title for title.

so.text: Each line is the conclusion its own page shows; the policy calculator applies either rule set to these figures.

note.text: A target is a level the town plans toward; a guideline of behavior is how money is set aside or spent. Which is which is our reading. Dollars apply each rule to the latest published figures.

blocks.title: Every policy, and what it changes

paragraphs.text: Both rules word for word, how the reserves have moved against them, the retiree health liability, and every meeting in the record.
This project recommends neither direction: not to save more, and not to spend more. The pages show what each rule set would do to figures the town has published. The boards decide.
